weather.insight: Clear operating window. Good day to front-load external meetings and site movement.

opening.verse_of_the_day: But seek first God’s Kingdom, and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well. — Matthew 6:33

anomaly.desc: JCI / IHSG spike of +1.92%; Nasdaq drop of -1.55%

market: JCI surged 1.92% to 6,037.84, decoupling from Nasdaq's 1.55% drop.
Commodity stocks drove Jakarta's gains while US tech sold off.
economic: BI hiked rates 25bp to 5.75% as Rupiah weakened to 18,100 per dollar.
Gold held near 4,009 and Brent crude slipped 0.14% amid geopolitical risk.
tech_ai: Google redesigned its search box for the first time in 25 years.
Railway raised $100 million to build AI-native cloud infrastructure challenging AWS.
political: Trump proposed a 20% toll on cargo through the Strait of Hormuz, raising energy security premiums.
Dubai plans a new port to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, altering trade routes.

arbiter_brief: Overnight US weakness will pressure JCI's tech proxies, but Jakarta's resilience hinges on commodity tailwinds. Coal and nickel gains counter foreign selling, while the Rupiah's slide and BI's hike raise capital costs. The Strait of Hormuz threat boosts Indonesia's strategic commodity exports, driving foreign rotation into resource plays, not tech.
executive_brief: Lock in commodity exposure to hedge against US tech rotation.
Prepare for tighter venture capital as US funds retreat from SEA.
Monitor Rupiah and BI rate trajectory for project cost implications.

sectors.name: Technology
sectors.ai: Indonesia's tech sector outperformed the US today, led by KONI's 25% surge and broad gains across digital infrastructure names. This signals growing domestic demand for connectivity and digital services, making selective exposure to local platform and data-center plays attractive for capturing structural growth while US tech headwinds persist.
themes: Digital infrastructure investment is accelerating in Indonesia as rising internet penetration and data consumption drive demand for data centers, cloud services, and fiber networks, creating durable r

Government push for digital transformation and financial inclusion is boosting adoption of fintech, e-commerce, and digital payment platforms, providing long-term tailwinds for companies with strong l

themes: Digital banking adoption in Indonesia is accelerating, driven by rising smartphone penetration and a young, unbanked population, benefiting players like ARTO.
Non-bank financial institutions (NICK, TUGU) are gaining traction as alternative credit sources amid tighter bank lending standards.
Insurance and multi-finance subsectors (BFIN, STAR) face margin pressure from rising claims costs and regulatory caps on lending rates.

sectors.name: Mining & Energy
sectors.ai: Indonesia's mining & energy sector shows selective strength, with coal and nickel plays leading on resilient demand and favorable policy signals. Focus on AMMN and UNTR as core holdings for exposure to copper/gold and coal, while monitoring SQMI and AGII for speculative momentum. Maintain WATCH for potential pullback entry points.
themes: Nickel downstreaming policy continues to drive value-add investments, supporting integrated players like AMMN with long-term pricing power.
Coal remains a cash cow for Indonesia, with UNTR benefiting from stable export demand and cost advantages despite global energy transition headwinds.
Regulatory clarity on mining permits and local processing requirements is creating structural winners among mid-cap miners like AGII and SQMI.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
sectors.ai: Indonesia's renewables sector shows strong local momentum (+3.23%) vs US flatness, signaling domestic policy tailwinds and EV/battery supply chain demand. VKTR's 25% surge underscores electric bus adoption, while BRPT and TOBA gains reflect geothermal and nickel-linked plays. Watch for sustained regulatory support and project financing catalysts.
themes: Indonesia's nickel downstreaming policy continues to drive battery and EV ecosystem investments, benefiting companies like BRPT and TOBA in the integrated supply chain.
Geothermal energy expansion remains a durable structural theme, supported by government targets for 35 GW renewable capacity by 2030, lifting PGEO and INPS.
Domestic electric vehicle adoption, particularly in public transport, is accelerating via mandates and subsidies, directly boosting VKTR and MPOW as key beneficiaries.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
sectors.ai: Indonesia Consumer & FMCG slipped 0.87% (ID -0.60%, US -1.36%), but selective names surged—JELI +24.91% and NTBK +7.69%—signaling rotation into small-cap value plays. Watch for further divergence as domestic demand stabilizes while US exposure drags; position into local champions with pricing power and distribution moats.
themes: Rising middle-class consumption in Java and Sumatra drives durable demand for branded FMCG staples, insulating local players from global slowdowns.
Government push for downstream agro-processing (e.g., palm oil derivatives, food ingredients) creates structural cost advantages for integrated Indonesian consumer firms.
Digital distribution and direct-to-consumer channels are widening margins for nimble local brands, eroding legacy multinationals' market share in tier-2/3 cities.

sectors.name: Infrastructure
sectors.ai: Indonesia's infrastructure sector slipped 1.32% today, but selective plays like KOKA (+23%) and HALO (+8%) signal rotation into niche contractors. Watch for sustained government capex push and toll road expansions to drive re-rating; avoid broad exposure until volume confirms a bottom.
themes: Government's accelerated infrastructure spending under the new cabinet will drive order books for mid-cap contractors like KOKA and MIRA, creating durable earnings visibility.
Toll road and port development remain structural catalysts, with regulatory easing on land acquisition unlocking multi-year project pipelines for firms like CTBN and APEX.
Foreign capital inflows into Indonesia's infrastructure are cyclical but tied to commodity prices; SCCO and VRT benefit from mining-related infrastructure demand as nickel and copper output expands.

macro_analysis.point: Escalating US-Iran tensions, including Trump's proposed 20% toll on Strait of Hormuz cargo and US strikes, have spiked the VIX by 14% and pressured global equities, with the Nasdaq falling 1.55%. This risk-off sentiment strengthens the US dollar index (+0.32%) and pushes US 10Y yields higher (+4bp), which in turn weighs on the rupiah (USD/IDR +0.20% to 18,100) and could deter foreign flows into Indonesian equities despite JCI's 1.92% gain.

BI's surprise 25bp rate cut to 5.75% (news index 4) has boosted domestic sentiment, driving JCI up 1.92% and supporting rate-sensitive sectors like property (+1.23%) and financials (+0.50%). However, the rupiah's depreciation to 18,100 amid a stronger dollar and rising US yields suggests the cut may pressure the currency, potentially limiting further easing and creating a headwind for import-heavy tech stocks.

Big Tech's push for AI data centers (news 3, 7, 8) is driving up power costs and demand for energy, benefiting Indonesian coal and nickel exporters. Coal proxy ITMG rose 2.68% and nickel proxy INCO gained 1.07%, as the US rally for utilities and data centers signals sustained commodity demand, while the mining & energy sector (+0.81%) outperformed.

The key risk is the interplay between Fed rate hike signals (news 14) and BI's rate cut: if US inflation data remains sticky and the Fed tightens further, the dollar could strengthen, exacerbating rupiah weakness and reversing JCI gains. This could particularly hit duration-sensitive tech stocks, which already fell 0.60%, and test the sustainability of Indonesia's rate-driven rally.
